sources.quote: There was wide variability in enforcement activities depending on the state, the region, and the lead inspecting agency.
sources.searcher_note: OIG report 26-E-0025 on RCRA large-quantity-generator enforcement 2020-2024, broken out by EPA region (Appendix B). Its table shows the share of violations with an enforcement action at Region 6 98%, Region 9 96%, Region 7 77%, Region 8 94%, i.e. Regions 6/9 do NOT look worse on this measure. Different measure (violations with any action, LQGs only, 2020-2024) from the lead (sites inspected twice with no case or informal action on file, all RCRA sites, since 2015). Report also says Region 9 data are incomplete because California data were missing, and that Region 6 was the only region where under half of formal actions carried a penalty.

sources.quote: state enforcement programs frequently do not meet national goals and states do not always take necessary enforcement actions.
sources.searcher_note: OIG report 12-P-0113, 'EPA Must Improve Oversight of State Enforcement'; covers RCRA among three statutes; general pattern that enforcement follow-up is weak and inconsistent across states and regions. No region-by-region inspected-but-no-action figure.

notes: No news or trade-press coverage found of an inspected-twice-with-no-action gap between EPA Regions 6/9 and 7/8. The closest source is the April 2026 EPA OIG regional table, which measures something different (share of LQG violations that drew any enforcement action, 2020-2024) and on that measure Regions 6 and 9 are near the top (98%, 96%), not the bottom; Region 7 is lowest of the four (77%). The judge should decide whether that counts as disagreement or a different definition. The OIG also flags Region 9 as incomplete because California data were missing, which may bear on the lead's Region 9 figure.
